name: Jane Eyre
kicker: Charlotte Brontë’s 1847 novel · An orphaned governess and a secret in the attic
briefing: Charlotte Brontë published _Jane Eyre_ in 1847 under the male-sounding pen name Currer Bell. It follows a poor, plain-spoken orphan who survives a cruel aunt and a harsh boarding school to become a governess at gloomy Thornfield Hall, where she falls for her brooding employer, Mr. Rochester. Just as the two are about to marry, Jane uncovers a shocking secret locked away upstairs.

sample.note: the 10 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: Midway through this novel, Mr. Rochester disguises himself as an old gypsy fortune-teller to draw out the heroine’s true feelings. Later, a visitor from Jamaica interrupts the heroine’s wedding before it can be completed.
tossups.r: That visitor’s sister, kept secretly in Thornfield Hall’s attic, turns out to already be Rochester’s wife. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title governess eventually marries Mr. Rochester, by Charlotte Brontë.

tossups.p: As a child, the heroine of this novel is nursed by the kindly apothecary Mr. Lloyd after she faints from fear in a locked room at her aunt’s house. Years later, this novel’s heroine is told by the housekeeper that strange noises in the house come only from a servant named Grace Poole.
tossups.r: That servant is secretly guarding Rochester’s insane first wife, Bertha Mason, in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title character becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall.

tossups.p: The woman kept hidden in this novel’s Thornfield Hall is a wealthy Creole heiress whom Rochester married in Jamaica years before meeting this novel’s heroine. A term describing that hidden first wife, “the madwoman in the attic,” later gave its name to a famous 1979 book of feminist literary criticism.
tossups.r: That woman, Bertha Mason, eventually burns Thornfield down. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title orphan marries the widowed Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: After fleeing Thornfield Hall, this novel’s heroine inherits a fortune from her uncle in Madeira, which makes her financially independent. This novel’s heroine first meets her future husband when his horse slips on ice near Thornfield and he sprains his ankle.
tossups.r: That same man, Mr. Rochester, later has his sight damaged when his hidden first wife burns down his house. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title governess returns to marry the blinded Rochester.

tossups.p: A childhood friend of this novel’s heroine, Helen Burns, teaches her patience and faith shortly before dying of consumption during a typhus outbreak at a harsh charity school. This novel is often praised as an early feminist work for its plain-spoken, independent heroine.
tossups.r: That heroine works as a governess at Thornfield Hall in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title character marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is nursed by the apothecary Mr. Lloyd after fainting in a locked room at her aunt Mrs. Reed’s house, Gateshead Hall. She is then sent to the harsh Lowood School, run by the stingy Mr. Brocklehurst.
tossups.r: There, she befriends Helen Burns, who dies of consumption during a typhus epidemic. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title orphan becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall.

tossups.p: A missionary named St. John Rivers proposes a loveless marriage to this novel’s heroine so she will join him on a mission to India; she refuses him. Earlier in this novel, Rochester disguises himself as a gypsy fortune-teller to test the heroine’s feelings for him.
tossups.r: Rochester’s guest Blanche Ingram is a rival the heroine wrongly fears he will marry instead. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title governess eventually marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is told by the housekeeper Mrs. Fairfax that strange laughter and noises come only from the servant Grace Poole. A visitor from Jamaica named Richard Mason arrives at Thornfield Hall and is injured by that same hidden figure in this novel.
tossups.r: Richard Mason later interrupts a wedding in this novel, revealing that the groom is already married to Richard’s sister, Bertha. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel about a governess who marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is raised by her unkind aunt, Mrs. Reed, at Gateshead Hall and is locked in the Red Room as punishment. Diana and Mary Rivers later take in this novel’s heroine after she flees Thornfield Hall, and the three turn out to be cousins.
tossups.r: Their brother, St. John Rivers, proposes marriage to the heroine as a missionary partnership; she refuses him. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title character eventually marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: Bertha Mason, a wealthy Creole woman Rochester married years earlier in Jamaica, is kept hidden in this novel’s Thornfield Hall by the servant Grace Poole. This novel’s heroine first meets Rochester after his horse slips on ice and he sprains his ankle.
tossups.r: Bertha eventually sets Thornfield on fire, blinding Rochester, in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title orphan returns to marry Rochester despite his injuries.

tossups.p: As a girl, this novel’s heroine is locked in the Red Room by her cruel aunt, Mrs. Reed, then sent to the harsh Lowood School under Mr. Brocklehurst. There she befriends Helen Burns, who dies of consumption during a typhus outbreak.
tossups.r: The heroine grows up to work as a governess at Thornfield Hall in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title character marries the widowed Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine inherits money from an uncle in Madeira and learns at the same time that she is cousin to Diana, Mary, and St. John Rivers. Rochester once disguised himself as an old gypsy fortune-teller to learn this novel’s heroine’s true feelings.
tossups.r: St. John Rivers proposes a loveless, missionary marriage to the heroine, who refuses him, in this novel. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title governess eventually marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: The critical term “the madwoman in the attic” describes a hidden character in this novel who is revealed during a wedding to be the groom’s first wife. This novel’s heroine is nursed by the apothecary Mr. Lloyd as a child after fainting in a locked room.
tossups.r: That heroine later befriends the dying Helen Burns at the harsh Lowood School in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title character marries Mr. Rochester.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is praised by critics as an early feminist figure for insisting on equality with the wealthy man she loves. A visitor from Jamaica, Richard Mason, is injured at Thornfield Hall and later stops this novel’s wedding from being completed.
tossups.r: Richard Mason’s sister, Bertha, turns out to already be married to Rochester in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel about a governess who marries Mr. Rochester after his house burns down.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is raised at Gateshead Hall by her unkind aunt, Mrs. Reed, before being sent to Lowood School under the stingy Mr. Brocklehurst. Grace Poole, a servant in this novel, is wrongly blamed for noises actually made by the insane Bertha Mason.
tossups.r: Bertha Mason burns down Thornfield Hall and blinds Rochester in this novel. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Brontë novel in which the title orphan marries Mr. Rochester.

trap.title: Which Brontë, which heroine?
trap.body: Charlotte Brontë wrote this novel, but her sister Emily Brontë wrote _Wuthering Heights_, a different Gothic romance with its own wild moor and its own doomed couple, Heathcliff and Catherine. This heroine is also sometimes mixed up with Jane Austen, a different, earlier author who never wrote about Thornfield Hall or a madwoman in the attic.
trap.fix: If the clue says Heathcliff, Catherine Earnshaw, or Thrushcross Grange, that is Emily Brontë’s novel, not this one. If it says Darcy, Elizabeth Bennet, or a Bennet family, that is Jane Austen, a different writer altogether.
